patterns: what is why is my phone slow
explain why is my phone slow
definition of why is my phone slow
why is my phone slow meaning
how to speed up my phone
entries.answer: A phone gets slow for reasons that are usually about the amount of work being asked of limited memory, and the first thing to check is how full the storage is, because a nearly full drive is a genuinely common cause and is free to fix. A phone keeps a running list of everything running, including things assumed to be idle, and a small amount of unused memory is what it needs to do ordinary things like opening a list. Background activity is the other half: apps left switched on for messages, location and synchronisation keep the processor awake, and on an older device that is the difference between smooth and unusable. Updates help more than people expect, because manufacturers fix performance problems in them, and the opposite advice, to install a cleaner app, is mostly a way to create a second problem. The honest summary is that a phone from several years ago will not be made fast by anything except less running at once.

patterns: how do i back up my data
how do i back up my phone
entries.answer: A backup is a second copy of your data somewhere else, and the one detail that makes it a backup rather than a copy is that it is somewhere else. Data that is on one device and also on the machine it is plugged into has not been protected from the failure that actually destroys it, which is usually theft, a drop or a flood, and those take the plugged-in machine too. What matters most to protect is rarely the device and is the account: a phone can be replaced and a library of photographs cannot. Automatic backup to a cloud account is the default for most phones and solves most of the problem for someone who does not think about it, and the check worth doing is whether it is actually running rather than whether it has been enabled. The old advice about checking a backup by restoring it remains the only way to be certain, since a backup that fails silently looks exactly like one that is working.
